This is a petition filed by the petitioners u/s 166 Gowramma vs Abhishek Raj on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129423299/
1 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act and Rule 232 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules claiming for compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ with interest from respondents on account of death of Munisiddegowda in the road traffic accident.
JUDGMENT 2.

The petitioner's case in brief:
That on 1992021 at about 9.30 a.m., when Munisiddegowda was traveling as pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing No.TVS XL bearing reg.No.KA42W5476 from Narayanapura, Kodihalli side towards his land, Kanakapura side on the extreme side of the road, near Srinivasa S/o Chinnagirigowda land, Narayanapura village,
Kodihalli Kanakapura road, Kasaba hobli, Kanakapura, Ramanagara district, at that time, rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA 04HE6961 came from Kodihalli side towards Kanakapura side with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and endangering to human life, dashed against the deceased from hind portion.

Due to impact deceased had sustained severe injuries all over the body and soon after the accident, deceased was shifted to Government hospital, Kanakapura wherein after first aid treatment, further management referred to NIMHANS hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein deceased took treatment took treatment as an inpatient from 209 2021 to 2292021 and for expert treatment further shifted JUDGMENT to Victoria hospital wherein inspite of better treatment on 22 92021 Munisiddegowda succumbed to fatal injuries.

It is further stated that prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 55 years and was earning Rs.40,000/p.m., doing agriculture,
sericulture and also milk vending business at Narayanapura village and having 5 acres irrigation land and maintaining his family members.
Due to death do Munisiddegowda, petitioners lost caretaker.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.30 lakhs from the respondents.
3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 and 3 remained absent and placed exparte.

The respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement wherein contended that it is the primary duty of the insured to intimate the insurer, if his vehicle is involved in any accident causing injuries to third parties or making damage to any property as per the terms and conditions of the policy and Section 134(c) of MV Act.

Even it is mandatory for the jurisdictional police to intimate to the insurer by submitting necessary documents that were JUDGMENT seized during the course of investigation as per Section 158(c) of MV Act.
It is further contended that deceased Munisiddegowda was riding TVS XL motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner, without wearing helmet and was not holding DL, he was hit by unidentified vehicle.
Since the vehicle dashed to him was not found at the spot, the petitioners was implicated the motor cycle bearing No.KA04 HE6961 for the cause of accident.

The petitioner has not made insured and insurer and rider of the motor cycle TVS XL bearing No.KA42W5476 as parties to the case proceedings and not made driver of insured motor cycle bearing No.KA04HE6961 as a party to the proceedings.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

Gowramma vs Abhishek Raj on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129423299/
2

4. From the above said pleadings three issues are framed:
ISSUES

1. Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased Munisiddegowda S/o late Daddegowda sustained grievous injury in an accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider JUDGMENT of the bike bearing No.KA04HE 6961on 1992021 at about 9.30 a.m. at KKP Kodthalli road, near Narayanapura village, Kasaba hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara, he succumbed to the said injury?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal representative of the deceased?
3. Whether the petitioner are entitled for compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?

4. What Order or Award?
5.
The petitioner No.1 got examined herself as P.W.1 and got examined one witness as PW2 and Exs.P1 to P31 documents are marked.
The respondents have not lead either oral or documentary evidence.

6. Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
7.

My answers to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 & 2 : In the Affirmative, Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.4 :

As per final order for the following: JUDGMENT REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 : In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA 04HE6961, the petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW.1 and one eye witness got examined as PW2 and got marked 31 documents as ExP1 to 31 i.e.,FIR, complaint,
requisition, spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report, post mortem report and enclosures,
Inquest report, charge sheet, outpatient records, medical bills, admission intimation,
death certificate, adhar cards, Srinivasahalli milk producers cooperative sangha letter, statement, Silk department auction chit, receipt, voter ID, adhaar card,
receipts given by durga traders, discharge summary, DL, RC, insurance policy.

9. The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by one Srinivasa S/o Nagaraju police conducted a thorough and detailed investigation and filed ExP9 charge sheet against the accused No.1 Manchaiah rider of the Pulsar motor cycle bearing No.KA04 JUDGMENT HE6961 for the offenses punishable Gowramma vs Abhishek Raj on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129423299/
3 under Sec's.279, 304A of IPC holding that on 1992021 at about 9.30 a.m. accused drove his Pulsar motor cycle bearing No.KA04HE6961 in a rash and negligent manner from Kodihalli towards Kanakapura and hit to the hind portion of the moped motor cycle TVS XL bearing No.KA42W5476 which was driven by the Srinivas along with the deceased Munisiddegowda as a pillion rider.
10. Further petitioner has produced ExP4 spot mahazar and ExP5 sketch.
On perusal of which, it clearly shows that the spot of accident was the two way road and the accident has been taken place on the right side of the road.
further it clearly shows that the accident had been taken place where the interior cross road joins the main road.

Admittedly as per the evidence of the PW2 eye witness and the rider of the TVS moped,
he was turning towards the cross road to go to his field.
As per the sketch, ExP5 the accident had been taken place on the right edge of the road where interior cross road joins the main road that means PW2 had already crossed the main road.
When the rider of the JUDGMENT offending pulsor vehicle was proceeding from Kodihalli towards Kanakapura why he came to the extreme right side of the road is not clear.

Thus from the evidence of the PW2 and the documents produced by the petitioner, it clearly shows that the accident had been taken place as the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA04HE6961 came towards extreme right side of the road.

Though counsel for respondent No.2 disputed the involvement of the vehicle and contended that accident has been place due to the rash and negligence of the deceased, but counsel for the respondent No.2 has not at all disputed the police document especially ExP35 and 9.
Further even respondent No.2 has not examined the rider of the pulsor motor cycle i.e., respondent No.3 to disprove the evidence of the PW1 and 2.
Even though respondent No.1 and 3 have not filed the written statement and objected and also not adduced any evidence in support of his contention.
11. Apart from this, on perusal of IMV report marked at ExP6, it reveals that on that day the accident has not caused due to the any mechanical defect of the above said JUDGMENT vehicles.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of the rider of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA04HE6961 and Munisiddegowda died the said accident.
As such, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
12. ISSUES NO.2 & 3 :
The petitioners have produced ExP13death certificate, ExP26voter ID card, ExP27 Adhaar card, ExP14 and 15Adhaar card of petitioner No.1 and 2.
From the said documents, it reveals that petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased Munisiddegowda.

13. This relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents,
as is evident from the tenor of cross examination of PW.1.

Be that as it may, since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the JUDGMENT deceased.

4 14.
LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS:
In the PM report (Ex.P.8) the age of the deceased is shown as 58 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '9'.
15.

The petitioners have stated that the deceased was doing agriculture and sericultural works and also milk vending work at Narayanapura village and having 5 acres irrigation land and earning Rs.40,000/p.m.

In support of their contentions, petitioners have produced ExP16 letter from the Srinivasa halli milk producers cooperative society Ltd., which reveals that deceased Munisiddegowda was supplying 18 to 21 milk every day and receiving Rs.9,000/ to Rs.10,000/
per day.

entities.text: Srinivasa halli milk producers cooperative society Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further petitioner has produced bank statement of Bangalore DCC bank Ltd., Kanakapura and the bank statement of Union Bank of India as per ExP19 and produced Sericulture 29 bid receipts and two bills of fruit and vegetables as per ExP20.
Further produced ExP21 and JUDGMENT 22 bills in respect of poultry form.
Further produced ExP23 and 24 bills of selling banana to the APMC market.

Thus from the above said documents, though it is clear that deceased was doing agriculture and dairy business and also Sericulture, but from these documents, this tribunal cannot ascertain the actual income derived by the deceased as petitioner has produced only bank statement, but petitioner has not proved what was the actual income by producing any cogent documents.
As such this tribunal is inclined to consider the notional income.
As the accident took place in the year 2021, the notional income of the deceased is taken as Rs.15,000/ p.m.
Needless to mention that age of the deceased, nature of his work as well as the present cost of living is also taken into consideration for ascertaining income.

16. In a decision reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others),
the Hon'ble Apex Court held that addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on JUDGMENT guesswork in the absence of proof of income.

entities.text: 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Sarala Verma's case towards his future prospectus if 10% of the salary is added it would be around Rs.16,500/ (15000 + 1500).
The deceased was married and having three dependents.
Hence 1/3rd of his income needs to be deducted towards personal & living expenses.
1/3 of Rs.16500/ works out to Rs.5500/.
Income for consideration is Rs.11000/ (16500 - 5500).
Annual income works out to Rs.1,32,000/ (11000 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '9'.
Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.11,88,000/ (1,32,000 X 9).
17. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In view of the ratio laid by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2021) 11 SCC 780 between United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others, each of the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/ (in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.40,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 JUDGMENT years from 2017) on account of loss of spousal consortium, parental consortium and loss of love & affection.

Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/ ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.15,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards loss of estate.
19. FUNERAL EXPENSES:
Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/ ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case, 10% of Rs.15,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards funeral expenses.

5 20.
The petitioners have stated that they spent Rs.3 lakhs including transportation, hospitalization charges etc.,

In support of their contention, petitioners have produced Ex P10outpatient records,
ExP11medical bills for Rs.1,32,554/, ExP12admission intimation.
Hence petitioners are entitle for compensation of Rs.1,32,554/ under the head medical expenses.
JUDGMENT 21.

The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of 11,88,00000 Dependency 2 Loss of 96,80000 Consortium 3 Loss of Estate 18,15000 4 Funeral 18,15000 Expenses 5 Medical 1,32,55400 expenses Total 14,53,654=00
The said total amount of Rs.14,53,654/ is rounded off to Rs.14,53,700/.
Hence, petitioners are entitle for compensation of Rs.14,53,700=00.
22. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

23. Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner, respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle and respondent No.3 is the insurance policy holder cum rider of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the JUDGMENT aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative' and issue No.3 is answered as 'Party in the affirmative'.
24. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the findings given on issues No.1 to 3 and for the reasons discussed therein, I proceed to pass the following;
: ORDER : The petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle's Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.14,53,700=00 with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

JUDGMENT On deposit together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 70  %
 Petitioner No.2 30  %
Gowramma vs Abhishek Raj on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129423299/
6

Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 a sum equal to 40% shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 5 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to her through Epayment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner No.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
After deposit, the entire compensation amount together with interest shall be released to the petitioner No.2 through Epayment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw an award accordingly.
